'''Anna Bruce Nevius''' is a retired American [[biostatistics|biostatistician]] who worked for many years in the [[Center for Veterinary Medicine]] of the US [[Food and Drug Administration]], and chaired the Biopharmaceutical Section of the [[American Statistical Association]].

==Early life and education==
Nevius is originally from North Carolina, and graduated from high school in 1961 in [[Murphy, North Carolina]]. As a mathematics major at [[Carson–Newman College]] in Tennessee, she discovered her interest in statistics by taking a course in the subject in her senior year.{{r|wis}}

She began a doctoral program in statistics at [[Kansas State University]],{{r|wis}} but after marrying fellow statistics student S. Edward Nevius in 1968,{{r|alum}} she left with a master's degree to follow her husband to Alaska, where he was posted from 1968 to 1970 by the [[United States Public Health Service]].{{r|wis|alum}} In the early 1970s, she and her husband moved to Florida, where he earned a doctorate in statistics from [[Florida State University]].{{r|ed}}

From 1975 to 1978 she worked as an instructor and statistical consultant in mathematics and statistics at the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln]], where her husband had a tenure-track faculty position. After her husband moved to the Food and Drug Administration in 1979, she returned to graduate study at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]],{{r|alum}}
and completed a Ph.D. in applied statistics in 1984.{{r|wis}} Her dissertation, ''Techniques for Combining <math>2\times 2</math> Contingency Tables: A Simulation Study'', was supervised by C. Mitchell Dayton.{{r|mg}}

==Career and later life==
Nevius entered government service working for the [[Internal Revenue Service]], but soon shifted to the Center for Veterinary Medicine, where she remained for the rest of her career.{{r|wis}} She chaired the Biopharmaceutical Section of the American Statistical Association for 2009.{{r|biopharm}} She retired three times and was rehired twice; after her second retirement, in 2022,{{r|omums22}} and her husband's death at the end of 2022,{{r|ed}} she returned to the center again in 2023 as a rehired annuitant.{{r|omums23}}

==Recognition==
Nevius was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2012.{{r|alum|fasa}}
